reasons: Grounded in the quoted behavior of registering attacker-controlled MFA after account compromise (T1556.006). It adds risky-sign-in correlation the evidence does not state, but this is a reasonable proxy.

Tables and columns exist and the syntax is valid, but the logic is flawed. The join filter is an OR, so any registration within 4h of any sign-in with singleFactorAuthentication matches, which is very broad. The ActorIp match is also unreliable, since a legitimate user's own same-IP sign-in followed by registration is the normal enrollment flow. TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName is not a reliably populated path, and tostring of a missing value gives an empty string, not null, so coalesce never falls back to Actor. The join is on UPN with no pre-aggregation and the union of 7d sign-ins is heavy. Non-interactive sign-ins are not covered.

An analyst can run it and the projected columns are useful for triage. However, the single-factor and same-IP branches will produce many benign hits. There is no summarization or dedup, so one registration can return many rows. There is no baseline for a new-method or new-device comparison.

A confidence of 45 is moderate and acknowledges the false positives. But the rationale calls same-IP sign-in a strong pattern, when same-IP is the benign norm, and the false-positive list omits the many noisy matches from the broad OR condition. The tuning advice partly compensates but does not match the query's real breadth.
